1.s: Paul thanks God for the Philippians’ partnership. His imprisonment has advanced the gospel. “For to me to live is Christ, and to die is gain.”
1.d: “He who began a good work in you will complete it until the day of Jesus Christ” [[bible:Philippians 1:6]]. It is God who begins his saving work in people, so we can trust him to finish it [[tosn:Philippians 1:6]].

2.s: Have the mind of Christ, who “emptied himself, taking the form of a servant”, humbled himself to death on a cross, and was highly exalted, “that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow.”
2.d: 2:6–11 is an early Christian hymn: Christ existed as God before the world began, came as a man and died, and was exalted as Lord over all [[tosn:Philippians 2:6-11]]. Epaphroditus risked his life for Christ on their behalf [[tosn:Philippians 2:29-30]].

3.s: Paul counts all his credentials as loss “for the excellency of the knowledge of Christ Jesus”. “I press on toward the goal.”
3.d: Paul was circumcised on the eighth day as the law required, and belonged to the Pharisees [[tosn:Philippians 3:5]]. Yet “I consider those things that were gain to me as a loss for Christ” [[bible:Philippians 3:7]].

4.s: “Rejoice in the Lord always!” “In nothing be anxious, but in everything, by prayer and petition with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God,” and his peace will guard your hearts. “I can do all things through Christ.”
4.d: “I have learned in whatever state I am, to be content in it” [[bible:Philippians 4:11]]. Paul’s life was full of the joy of doing God’s will whatever the cost [[tosn:Philippians 4:11-12]]. Thinking on what is true, noble and lovely is part of having the mind of Christ (2:5) [[bsn:Philippians 4:1-9]].
